text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A suspect in the 96 million shillings ($1.7 million) Standard Chartered Bank heist of February says police recovered more money from his house than they said they had.
- There is no let-up in the road accident toll with nine more people dying within the last two days.
- The National Convention Planning Committee says the election boycott call by some opposition leaders is shortsighted.
- The British High Commission in Kenya cautions against using racial tensions as a playing card to gain electoral advantage.
- A suspected witch is caught bewitching a neighbour's child in a residential estate in Mombasa.
- The Italian community at the Kenyan coast meet amid public outrage over revelations of a Mafia-style tax evasion and illegal immigration ring run by powerful members of the community.
- Assistant Minister in the office of the president, Japheth Shamalla, says he has evidence that opposition parliamentarian Paul Muite is related to Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
- The Roman Catholic Church says no political leader should play up racial or ethnic tension to earn political mileage.
- A syndicate where fake documents are being used to release suspects from Shimo-La-Tewa Maximum Prison in Mombasa is uncovered by police.
